properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised 2026-08-04 alongside dec:idea-retrospective-review-skill, of which this is the shape question rather than the whether question. THE FORK. OPTION A — A QUESTION LIST. The skill carries Anthony's sixteen questions as prose and the agent answers them by reading the design and the code. Cheap to build, works on day one, works on any project regardless of what the graph holds, and is what a human reviewer actually does. The objection is precise and comes from reflow2's own record: BL-179 settled that reflow2 does not encode a good practice as a detector, because Anthony objected that "avoid monoliths" is "kind of a subjective ask" — and the resolution was that reflow2 reports where two records the design ALREADY HOLDS disagree and rules on neither side. Sixteen prose questions answered by an agent is subjective grading with a checklist in front of it, and the answers would vary by model, by session, and by how much of the codebase happened to fit in context. OPTION B — EVERY QUESTION BACKED BY A COMPUTATION. Each question maps to a reading that already exists or is buildable over records the graph holds, and any question with no such reading reports NOT INFORMED with the reason instead of inviting an opinion. This is exactly ility_report's discipline (BL-184) turned into a skill, and the mapping is largely already there: "too joined together" is modularity, misplaced capabilities and god-components; "did the build separate what the design distinguishes" is granularity_report; "what did we leave until last" is maturity_report's frontier; "what happens if a key part breaks" is articulation points and single points of failure; "can others read and change this" is partly coverage_report and the unregistered regions. The cost is that Anthony's speed-and-efficiency group and most of his security group have NO computation behind them today and would honestly report NOT INFORMED — which looks like a weaker skill and is a more honest one. OPTION C — THE CENSUS SHAPE, which is what actually produced BL-198..BL-203 and is neither A nor B. It asks nothing and grades nothing: it diffs artifacts the project maintains SEPARATELY and expects to agree — the schema against the graph against the tool surface, and the practice the skills PRESCRIBE against the practice the graph FOLLOWS. It surfaces disagreements and leaves every verdict to the human, which is precisely the BL-179 resolution generalised beyond detectors. Its limit is equally precise: it can only find a disagreement between two records that BOTH EXIST, so it is blind to anything nobody wrote down, and it says nothing about Anthony's speed, security or bad-input groups at all. AN HONEST OBSERVATION ABOUT THE THREE: they are not exclusive, and the census is the only one of them with evidence behind it today — six rows in one sitting, one of which (BL-199) explained a hard blocker that eleven releases of green instruments had missed. A plausible synthesis is C as the engine, B as the reporting discipline, and A kept only as the part a human is asked, never the part an agent answers. Nobody has chosen. NOT ASKED HERE, AND IT MAY MATTER MORE THAN THE FORK: whether a retrospective is worth anything when run by the same agent that built the thing. The census was, and its blind spot was real — BL-199 was found by a mechanical three-way diff, not by the agent noticing it had done something wrong.
properties.name: OPEN — should a retrospective review ASK its questions or COMPUTE them, and is it ever allowed to grade?
properties.rationale: Kept separate from dec:idea-retrospective-review-skill because one node holding two unrelated questions can never be answered, only half-answered. That node asks whether the skill should exist; this one asks what it would have to be to survive reflow2's own rule against subjective grading. Not registered as formal alternatives: registering them would make this a fork with a design behind each branch and start the loop asking Anthony to choose, which is exactly what a brainstorm should not do.
